newsitem.title: USA: Freddie Mac prices preferred shares at $50.
newsitem.headline: Freddie Mac prices preferred shares at $50.

text.p: Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp on Thursday said it priced an offering of 12 million shares of fixed-rate, perpetual preferred stock at $50 each, with a coupon of 6.14 percent.
The government-sponsored agency, known as Freddie Mac, has the option to redeem the shares on June 30, 2002.

The shares are expected to be issued on June 3. For up to 18 months that date, Freddie Mac will increase the dividend if the U.S. tax code is amended to reduce the dividends-received deduction to as low as 50 percent from the current 70 percent.
The proceeds are to be used for general corporate purposes, including the purchase of residential mortgages, Freddie Mac said in a news release.

The underwriters, led by Goldman Sachs & Co, include Salomon Brothers Inc; Bear, Stearns & Co; Lehman Brothers Inc; Blaylock & Partners LP; Merrill Lynch, Pierce Fenner & Smith Inc; J.P. Morgan Securities Inc and Morgan Stanley & Co Inc.
